steps.text: Scar Market, Kazdel

steps.name: Wounded Mercenary
steps.text: You protect this tag around your neck with your bLIFE! You're MY precious property, slave!

steps.name: Wounded Mercenary
steps.text: You understand?! *Sarkaz swearing* You'd better be worth something.

steps.name: Wounded Mercenary
steps.text: Stay here and don't move. You, you inspect the goods?
The slave trader casts a glance at the silent slave behind the mercenary's back, then slightly shakes his head.

steps.name: Slave Trader
steps.text: Where'd you get it?

steps.name: Wounded Mercenary
steps.text: Found him on my way here, dying of thirst and about to become mangler chow. Thought he could fetch a good price.

steps.name: Timid Slave
steps.text: I... came from Kazdel... I can find someone who...

steps.name: Slave Trader
steps.text: Doesn't matter to us where you're from, slave. Say you're Higashinese for all we care, as long as someone buys you out.

steps.name: Slave Trader
steps.text: I'm just checking if you've got a tail. You never know where these mercs get their 'goods'.

spans.text: . You never know where these mercs get their 'goods'.

steps.name: Wounded Mercenary
steps.text: I promise you he's clean.

steps.name: Slave Trader
steps.text: You better not be messing with me. Cash or barter?

steps.name: Wounded Mercenary
steps.text: Ain't gonna live long enough for money to mean something. Give me some good weapons.

steps.name: Slave Trader
steps.text: You're the boss. He's second-rate, at best... that'll net you two blades, freshly cast.

steps.name: Wounded Mercenary
steps.text: How about you take another look, with your eyes open this time!

steps.name: Slave Trader
steps.text: You can dress him up as a first-rate, but it won't change anything. If you don't like our offer, feel free to get lost.

steps.name: Slave Trader
steps.text: And put that machete of yours away...

steps.name: Slave Trader
steps.text: This is the Scar Market you're in.

steps.name: Wounded Mercenary
steps.text: ...Can you throw in more? I was out on the Leithanien border before I got back, I've got first-hand intel about the whole war in the Core—

steps.name: Slave Trader
steps.text: Well, here's something for nothing: careful what you spew out of that mouth if you want to stay alive here.

steps.name: Slave Trader
steps.text: Mouthing around you have valuable 'first-hand intel'... You want to guess where that'll get you?

steps.name: Slave Trader
steps.text: Leave the goods and scram. You're holding up the line.

steps.name: Wounded Mercenary
steps.text: *grunt*.

steps.name: Slave Trader
steps.text: Not happy? Drown your sorrows in the bar. Our boss, Scareye, brews one heck of a drink. Doesn't matter if you can't pay your tab... they'll take your weapons as collateral, merc.

steps.name: Wounded Mercenary
steps.text: One more thing... where do you run your bounty board? I'm here to strike it rich.

steps.name: Slave Trader
steps.text: The barfolk'll be happy to inform you.

steps.name: Wounded Mercenary
steps.text: *Sarkaz swearing*.
The merc stares around this floating hub, hidden away in the giant subterranean hollow beneath Kazdel.
Amidst the moans of the slaves, the faint yet constant rumble of lava and bursts of Originium dust can be heard rising from beneath the market.
Eyeing the rugged path behind him, the mercenary recalls the perils he faced to reach here from the surface and shudders.

steps.name: Wounded Mercenary
steps.text: Just how many people are there in that goddamn... chasm?

steps.name: Slave Trader
steps.text: Enough to break your fall, if you jumped. Welcome to the Scar Market, greenhorn. You'll love it here.

steps.name: Wounded Mercenary
steps.text: What's the deal over there? Why the crowd?

steps.name: Slave Trader
steps.text: Probably another big name just rolled back into town.

steps.name: Slave Trader
steps.text: Aren't you here to 'strike it rich'? Go on, then. I'd rather keep my horns out of all that mess.
The merc vaguely makes out a pale white figure flitting through the chaotic gloom of the street.
White clothes? You don't see that everyday in Kazdel.
You're injured.

steps.name: Wounded Mercenary
steps.text: Tell me something I don't know.

steps.name: Slave Trader
steps.text: Gkh! *cough* *cough*! You're—
The last time I was here, it was someone else handling transactions.

steps.name: Slave Trader
steps.text: Guh. Yes...

steps.name: Slave Trader
steps.text: You're referring to my grandfather. He never stopped bragging about how he'd fought you and lived.

steps.name: Slave Trader
steps.text: I'm surprised you'd remember him. In the good sense, though, that means he wasn't lying all this time. It must've been sixty years ago by now...

steps.name: Slave Trader
steps.text: ...General Theresis.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Already? How sad that nothing here has changed at all.

steps.name: Slave Trader
steps.text: I imagine with Her Highness here, too, there'll be no more violence this time, eh?

steps.name: Slave Trader
steps.text: Even if things get bloody, eventually you'll leave, but we'll always be here, General. We'll always have business, so long as Kazdel's unrest never rests.

steps.name: Slave Trader
steps.text: Even now, I remember one thing my grandpa mentioned in his boasts. He said to you, it's the land of Kazdel that needs us.
Theresis looks at the slaves, their heads down in their cages. He draws his sword.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: War and turmoil have necessitated this trade for over a century... this Scar Market.

spans.text: War and turmoil have necessitated this trade for over a century... this

steps.name: Timid Slave
steps.text: G... General—I...

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Provided you can reach the surface alive... Take a fresh look at Kazdel.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Much of what you know will soon change. All Sarkaz will be part of this change.

steps.name: Slave Trader
steps.text: All? Us too?

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Yes. I'm not inclined to explain our vision to the likes of you. But I will stay here a while longer and wait for her return.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Until then, I welcome you mercenaries to challenge me, just as sixty years ago.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: I will take you to Kazdel, willingly or otherwise.
His voice isn't loud, but every Sarkaz present hangs onto his every word.
The mixed-blood Sarkaz stands alone—no retinue, no army—armed only with an ordinary-looking longsword, casually held in the hand that wields it.
His steely gaze pierces through the dim of the street, settling calmly in the direction of the only person he cares for.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You can dismiss the mercenaries in ambush. No doubt they're your most trusted men.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: This is out of my respect for the King of Sarkaz. None aside from the General can claim to know your true motives, after all.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Your Highness, do you truly believe this can change the fate of the Sarkaz? That you're not just another ill-fated hero caught in this cycle of hope and failure?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Once the dust has all settled, your answer will come naturally.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Following that pyrrhic victory, we built from zero a moving city, the great nomad of Sarkaz soil for over a century now.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: We can evade Catastrophes and foreign armies. Our development has finally reached a point of basic self-sufficiency. But it's so far from enough.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The storm has long been brewing on the horizon, but we were too oblivious, like a burdenbeast too slow to react, too old to move.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Your Highness must be referring to that war between Leithanien and Gaul.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Surely you, too, are aware of the magnitude of that war.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Corsica I even secretly hired our Royal Court Casters as his consultants, but despite a period of seclusion, Leithanien's Witch King thwarted Gaul's offenses with his opening move.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: And now, Ursus and Victoria have also declared war on Gaul.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: These present empires display a might so far removed from the enemy one hundred and thirty years ago, against which we staked all Kazdel just to barely prevail.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: That was already a victory in name only. If Kazdel must now be thrust into the same situation, how could it possibly end?

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: It is for this end that you wish to establish the 'Military Commission of Kazdel'.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Yet, the old aristocrats of the Royal Court grow resentful, refusing to relinquish their sumptuous city lives and viewing this as an attempt to challenge their privileges.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: A century of peace is enough for certain memories to slip their minds.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: So, what made you deign to come here in person? Do you see the 'Scar Market' as the 'Royal Court' for the bottom-feeders, where the likes of us scape by and make merry?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: My only hope is for more Sarkaz to join us and resist the voices that refuse to embrace change.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Resist? Perhaps your Highness meant 'terrorize' and 'purge'.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: What I want is a reform, not a slaughter.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: So, what's the reward?

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: The Scar Market's not a real Royal Court. What we have with the mercenaries is partnership, not fealty. Without compensation, no one will work for us.

spans.text: Royal Court. What we have with the mercenaries is partnership, not fealty. Without compensation, no one will work for us.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: ...Reward?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Are the spoils of war not enough? Are the riches, power, or food that should have gone to the hungry people not enough to sate your appetite?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You claim to provide shelter and a livelihood for countless Sarkaz warriors with your rhetoric of justice... Yet, I could almost hear their bones crunch as you squeeze them dry for profit.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Sorry, but in this business, we eat people whole and chew on their bones.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Scareye.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You too are Sarkaz. You too are a part of Kazdel.
While Theresa cannot see what expression lies behind Scareye's mask, his emotions are clear as day before her pitch-black crown.
No commoner in Kazdel would ever dare defy the Royal Court.
But in his emotions, all Theresa sees is fervor and bloodthirst.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You won't refuse.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: ...Hah.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Why would I? Do you think I'm scared they'll take revenge on me? The Royal Court's no mystery to me, Your Highness knows that plenty well.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: And let me say... You've promised me, no doubt... the best 'reward' I could ask for.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: We thrive on chaos, and I can 'see' the level of chaos you will bring upon Kazdel.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The fact that you've kept the name 'Scar' tells me that your ideas haven't changed.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Like you said, the nations of Terra have grown tremendously in power over the last century. We could throw more revenants into the Soul Furnace and stoke its flames, but it'll not close that gap.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: So why force the people, who aren't really of the same race, to band together, call themselves the Sarkaz, and build a giant target called 'Kazdel'?

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: The war between the four superpowers has proven that other Terra nations can accept our existence as mercenaries, and that's where Scar Market comes in.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: And Your Highness surely knows that we've become a community, a town, because many of us could never fit into the elitist, bloodline-obsessed Royal Court.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: In all these years, I may have helped just as many Sarkaz find a new way of life as the Six Heroes, if not even more.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: And I'm not the least bit ashamed to say it, Your Highness, King of Sarkaz.
Theresa doesn't reply. All she offers is a faint smile at the Cyclops.
Ah. It suddenly occurs to Scareye that this King of Sarkaz belongs to no Royal Court and represents no bloodline.
Her sole aim is to persuade the Sarkaz who are unwilling to believe that Kazdel can be built, some of whom have even committed crimes for this cause, to believe once more.
But is she enough to break free from this cycle of tragic failures, from the ending he foresaw?

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Come to think of it, there's one thing I don't get, Your Highness. I might have agreed to help you...

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: But why didn't you and General Theresis simply burn this place to the ground before the day's end? I would have little chance of winning if you decided to do so.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Just like you did sixty years ago.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: A minute ago, you described 'Kazdel' as nothing but a target and that you want another way for the Sarkaz to live, one that would have them depend on other nations.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: So tell me, in your prophetic visions, have you seen Kazdel's destruction?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Have you seen my death, Theresis's death, and the destruction of all that you stand against?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: And what about yourself? How do you behold your death? A slow and agonizing death by Oripathy? Slain in battle on foreign soil? Or drowned in a sea of plots and conspiracies?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Have you ever left this place, and seen Kazdel as it is now?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Have you ever truly seen 'the future'?

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Is this your way of asking for a prophecy? I don't give handouts, but for your Highness, I'll consider a discount.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Such nerve. No wonder you were able to claw your way out of this bleakness and rebuild this mercenary's paradise.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But I'll pass on the prophecy.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Prophecies and fate have no value.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: It's getting late. I look forward to your return to Kazdel.
He watches her go and heaves a long sigh only when even her footsteps fall from earshot.
Son of a bitch.
Foresight? Prophecies? His own death?
He bought his coffin this very morning.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Tally up the losses.

steps.name: Slave Trader
steps.text: Boss, the slaves...

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Set them free. They're bound to get tangled up in the Scar Market after the war begins anyway. At most, we lose out on pocket change.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Did anyone take on General Theresis and survive?

steps.name: Slave Trader
steps.text: Yes. I've noted them all down.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Take them to supplies for a little reward. They've got real balls.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: When you're done, take them to the bar entrance and kill 'em all in front of everyone. Send their heads to General Theresis as an apology.

steps.name: Slave Trader
steps.text: ...Got it.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Send their rewards to whatever family and friends they have as bereavement.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Tell every merc looking to make a living in the Scar Market, I don't want to see 'anyone' trying funny shit on my turf.
He heads alone to the bar, the tags on his cloak jangling in his steps.
He stands prominently in the crowd, watching as the blades take the light from the mercenaries' eyes.
Still, no one fights back.
Utter disappointment.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Drinks are on the house tonight, both to celebrate the two Highnesses sparing your lives...

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: And to celebrate the huge gig you've all just landed. Your objective... is in Kazdel.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Get your shit ready. Soon, you're all gonna be in the city.
Secret Entrance of Scar Market, Kazdel

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: You've been quiet for some while now, Theresa.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Are you hesitating?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: No, I have confidence in you. A reshuffle of the War Council is inevitable, it's just...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I've been thinking about the city's future. War won't stop itself at Gaul. Our pace has fallen too far behind.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Corsica I commands an indomitable fleet of dreadnoughts and guard battalions. The mad king of Leithanien has more than his Arts in his arsenal to effect Gaul's failure.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The industrial might of both Ursus and Victoria in the throes of a large-scale war has far surpassed our imaginations...

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Many assume to know war like the back of their hands simply by living long enough through it.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: If our concept of war still lingers on the great battle from a century ago, then we have drastically underestimated how quickly wars can nourish empires and fuel dictatorships.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: This is exactly why we need a Military Commission.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: It's more than that, Theresis.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: ...I know.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: When the day comes, when the Sarkaz wish to live on, if a brittle, creaking city is all they have to call their own—

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: It will be far from enough.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Do you remember the idea I proposed, back when Kal'tsit was designing the city's blueprints with us?

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Babel.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: To transcend the borders of race and nation. To echo far and wide in our ideals, in our epics.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: ...Founded by a Sarkaz.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: We will prepare Kazdel for the coming crisis, strive to eradicate the poverty and disease that have plagued them for millennia, and send a message to all of Terra.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: There will come a future when we all stand as one. The Sarkaz, too, are part of Terra's destiny.
This is not the first Theresis has heard of her idea.
Apart from the Dame who left after helping build the nomadic city of Kazdel many years ago, he alone knows the true belief of the current King of Sarkaz.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Kazdel won't accept this 'Babel', you and I both know that well.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: It's but a dream of attempting to subvert reality.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Yes... for now, at least, we can't be talking of such grand ideals while even our own affairs are slipping away from us.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: It's my hope this 'Babel' can become a part of Kazdel, Theresis.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Are you prepared, then?

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: As I said before, it's not just the other nations that will oppose you. Kazdel and the Sarkaz clinging to their hatred will also stand against you.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: It is cruel to force them to forgive and forget. The persecution of the Sarkaz is not history. The ancient hatred is what drives many to survive until this day.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I am the King of Sarkaz. The responsibility is all mine to bear. I must show them a way out of this.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: ...I see.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Then go. Do what you will.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Theresa, I still do not approve of your vision, but I do support your decision, and the future Military Commission will, too.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: If your gaze is set too far to see what lies before you, then I shall sweep away all that obstructs you at the moment, just as always.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Come, let's go home. Kazdel still needs us for what's about to happen.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Oh, yes. Scareye mentioned the prophecy again as I was leaving...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The signs of a pessimistic fate.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: And your reaction?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I don't care.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Agreed.
Kazdel—a strange yet familiar name.
Many from this great land see it as the pit from which devils crawl—a terrible place to be avoided at all costs.
While to the Sarkaz, the name only evokes equally conflicted emotions.
Despite generations of Sarkaz passing on that Kazdel is the Sarkaz's homeland, an outsider might wonder if they mean the city or the entirety of those lands?
Perhaps only they themselves know.

steps.name: Timid Slave
steps.text: It never struck me on the way out just how high this wall is... Oh well, at least I can go home alive now. That means I'm pretty lucky.

steps.name: Timid Slave
steps.text: That man in the Scar Market... that was General Theresis. The first of this city's founders, the hero of that legendary campaign.

steps.name: Timid Slave
steps.text: *sigh* If I had the courage to ask him to take me in, maybe I could've just...

steps.name: Timid Slave
steps.text: *sigh*... I'm dreaming again.
He sits atop the high wall, experiencing for the first time a new lease on life.
Few of Kazdel's civilian Sarkaz, save for those children who haven't yet cottoned onto the fear of death, ever climb onto the city wall.
If the tremendous pipes and tubes piled high can even be called a wall.
The intricately tangled 'forest' of Originium spikes can take the lives of anyone who loses their footing, but it also serves as a haven for pilferers and mercenaries to stash their goods.
Smugglers and vagrants cross through the dark underground, peeking out from the tunnels and drains at mines and factories, scuttling from one corner of the city to another.
The life the slave once knew.

steps.name: Timid Slave
steps.text: The General gave me a fresh start. So what should I do from now on...?
He gazes at the furnace, burning and smoldering far away, teeming with indiscernible workers as they carry Originium, steel, dirt and stones into its hearth.
To Kazdel the nomad, its flames bring motion, while the molten metal that flows out adds new appendage to the city.
For a whole century, it's belched its incessant black smoke. None know whether it's ash or Originium dust. Some say it's the bitter anger and anguish as the revenants exhale their last breaths.
Witchcraft altars hang high in the sky, intermittently flashing their blinding rays. The slave has heard many different versions of their urban legend.
The most frightening version claims that the Royal Court's casters work day and night on the altars, watching everything and listening to every conversation in the city.

steps.name: Timid Slave
steps.text: Maybe I can try my luck at the factories, too.

steps.name: Timid Slave
steps.text: It doesn't matter what else... I've made it back alive.

steps.name: Timid Slave
steps.text: It's been months since I left. I don't know how many of my friends are still alive...
The nomadic city of Kazdel, Kazdel

steps.name: Timid Slave
steps.text: *Sarkaz swearing* What happened here?

steps.name: Timid Slave
steps.text: Why are all the doors open and the furniture all smashed...

steps.name: Wary Civilian
steps.text: Pull-Top! You're back!

steps.name: Timid Slave
steps.text: It's you! What are you doing here? Where'd you get that ornament?

steps.name: Wary Civilian
steps.text: Something big is happening. Royal Court nobles are being dragged out of their houses and killed by mercenaries appearing from nowhere, while the city guards do nothing!

steps.name: Wary Civilian
steps.text: A lot of us have been sneaking into the empty houses, and boy, have we dredged up some good stuff!

steps.name: Wary Civilian
steps.text: How are you still alive, though? Word got out you wanted to leave the city and find your own way, and after so long, we all assumed you died out there.

spans.text: still alive, though? Word got out you wanted to leave the city and find your own way, and after so long, we all assumed you died out there.

steps.name: Timid Slave
steps.text: Heh. You won't believe my luck! First, I was left to die without food or water, then I was taken to the Scar Market... but guess what?

steps.name: Timid Slave
steps.text: General Theresis saved my life, the General himself! Then, on the way home, I ran into this guy with a halo over his head, calling himself a Messenger, and he brought me all the way back to the city wall.

steps.name: Timid Slave
steps.text: So, I've decided to change my name to Goodluck starting today. You guys can forget that lousy old name of mine.

steps.name: Wary Civilian
steps.text: Pft, a guy with a halo? A Sankta? And then the General? You sure learned how to lie, Goodluck.

spans.text: Pft, a guy with a halo? A Sankta? And then the General? You sure learned how to lie,

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: Believe me or don't, but either way, today is a fresh new start for me! I'm gonna go be a miner—

steps.name: Wary Civilian
steps.text: I looted a Nachzehrer's house earlier and found some hot air balloons. Wanna launch me on one and put that luck of yours to good use?

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: I'm in!

steps.name: Wary Civilian
steps.text: Well, that was fast.

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: Man, it feels good to be home.
Goodluck glances around at the people swarming the street. This is the life he knows.
If he wants to survive, the city will always offer him a way.

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: Thank you, fate, and thank you, General.
